action_summary: Round 15 audits the one word every receipt since round 9 has leaned on: 'the commit's own tests pass'. A fix has parts, and a passing suite can require some parts and be indifferent to the rest, so the audit is a real mutant that needs no synthetic data -- revert one part of the human's own change and run the suite. 16 real fixes, 77 suite executions, 45 parts: 30 parts are required and 30 of 42 behavioural parts are pinned (71.4%); six of sixteen fixes contain a behavioural part the suite would accept without; one tomli fix is reversible in seven of its eight parts while the suite stays green, because every part is an error message and the tests assert the exception type and never the message. One task refused because its controls did not hold, and is reported rather than counted. The finding is not that the suites are bad: it is that the certified share of a real change is a property of the assertions, so no amount of experience, retention or smarter action can raise it. The capability this yields is per-part certification -- the agent must report which parts of its own work are pinned and which are hypotheses -- and it names the next move: synthesise the assertion that would pin each unpinned part, which is the only change that strengthens the verifier instead of the agent's confidence.

obs_blocker.intrinsic_or_path_specific: intrinsic: what a set of observations determines is a fact about the action and the observations, not about the learner. Either the survivors agree on the states in reach or they do not.
obs_blocker.surviving_causal_blocker: One execution leaves a set of readings that agree on the observed state. For real actions that set is larger than one (343 readings in the grammar here, median 1037 candidate programs in the tree's coding measurement), and the readings part company only on states the observation never touched -- which is why the failure is invisible exactly where it happens.

obs_solution.efficiency_mechanism: Discovery costs one subprocess per (step, candidate path) and buys the difference between redoing 8 steps and redoing 14, or worse, redoing 1 wrong step and declaring the work repaired.
obs_solution.generality_mechanism: The rule is not about tar: any step is a function of the state it can see, so perturbing a candidate and comparing the consequence yields its read set on a GUI, a database or a network service with the matching probe.
obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Reading the read set off argv is wrong in both directions and fails 2 of 3 real chains; tracing requires infrastructure that does not exist here and annotates what must be discovered; asking a model is prohibited producer cognition; redoing everything works and costs 75% more, and does not tell the agent what to redo when the state is too large to rebuild.

The field's own direction is the same problem under other names -- the verifiability constraint (RLVR works only where a grader exists), OSWorld 2.0's finding that agents spend under 7% of budget on verification and skip it, and rubric-based reward construction, which is grader BUILDING, the cost centre everyone now names. route_frontier.why_selected_route_is_fastest_sufficient: It costs one instrument and settles the question that has made every previous zero ambiguous: how much of real change each mechanism can even address. It needs no new learner, no model and no network.
route_frontier.why_this_is_not_another_organ: It reuses the corpus, the judge and difflib, and it deletes the assumption that a passing suite certifies a change. The only new operation is reverting one part of the human's own change, which is cheaper than any mutant generator and is made of real work. It exists because the tree's mutation gate answers a different question (does a generated perturbation get observed) and its adequacy organ answers a third (would an unexecuted line be caught).
